messages:
From: Anna Ortiz <anna.ortiz@novahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Final pricing & PO routing — order form redlines

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the walkthrough yesterday. Attached is our annotated order form (order_form_v3_redlines.pdf) and a local copy of our pricing spreadsheet. A few things we need clarified before sending the PO to our procurement system: 

- We would like Net 90 payment terms (we have longer internal AP cycles).
- We requested a minimum commit reduction on year 1 from 500k to 350k (see appendix A on the PDF).
- VAT handling: Nova is in the EU; we'd like Redwood to accept an EU VAT reverse-charge flow and invoice our UK entity; we attached the VAT cert.
- We also asked for an indemnity carveout for data residency (MSA §9).

Can you confirm which of these are deal-breakers? We plan to route a PO once the order form language and the MSA redlines are agreed.

Best,
Anna Ortiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Nova Health

Attachments: order_form_v3_redlines.pdf (pdf), pricing_schedule_nov2026.xlsx (xlsx), vat_certificate_nova.pdf (pdf)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Final pricing & PO routing — requests from Nova (please advise)

Team — forwarding Nova's annotated order form. High level asks: Net 90, 350k mincommit Y1, VAT reverse-charge to their UK entity, and an MSA indemnity carveout for data residency.

Quick asks: 
- Legal: which of these are acceptable or require alternative language? Point me to exact MSA sections to propose.
- Finance: can we support Net 90 for this account (they're strategic)? If not, what's the latest we can go and any credit/collection conditions?
- Sales: recommended commercial concessions if we can't meet Net 90 (discounts, escrow, early-payment incentives).

I'll hold on replying to Anna until we have guidance.

-Jordan
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Final pricing & PO routing — legal guidance on redlines

Jordan / team — reviewed the PDF. Notes below referencing the MSA (v202602):

1) MSA §5 (Limitation of Liability): Nova added an exception for data residency; we cannot accept an open indemnity carveout. Proposal: add a narrowly scoped statement in the order form acknowledging their data residency requirement and committing to documented controls + SOC2 evidence within 30 days of signature. Do not change §5 in MSA.

2) Net 90: commercial term — legal can accept extended payment terms only with strengthened credit protections. If Finance approves Net 90, we need either: (a) a PO with an irrevocable payment schedule + staged invoices, or (b) a letter of credit/escrow for first tranche. We should capture this in Order Form Appendix B.

3) Mincommit: changing 500k -> 350k is a commercial decision. Legal flags language that would create an evergreen obligation if the mincommit drops; include a clause that unbilled usage above the reduced commit can be trued-up at renewal.

4) VAT reverse-charge: we can accept reverse-charge invoicing to their UK entity provided they supply a valid VAT registration and a signed self-billing agreement. We should not be responsible for VAT exposures if their certificate is invalid. Add explicit indemnity carve for VAT errors.

5) DocuSign: if they want the MSA amended, route change to legal signature page; otherwise capture all deal-specific deviations in the Order Form only.

I'll draft suggested order form language (tracked) and attach a short comment file.

-Kim
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02 15:00:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Fwd: Final pricing & PO routing — commercial tradeoffs

Agree with Kim. From a commercial standpoint: 

- Net terms: Nova is a strategic target but Net 90 materially increases DSO. Recommend counter to Net 60 + 20% upfront on year 1 activation and first month usage to cover ramp. That buys us 30 days vs Net 90 and lowers credit exposure.
- Mincommit: we can accept 350k year 1 if we make the reduction explicit and charge any shortfall at renewal or accelerate billing if usage is > commit. Also add a carve that allows Redwood to invoice for shortfall if they terminate early.
- VAT: require their VAT cert before we issue invoice. If they insist on reverse charge, we add the indemnity language Kim suggested.

If Finance signs off on Net 60 + 20% upfront, I can send a 'commercial compromise' note to Anna and push for PO.

-Ben
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Anna Ortiz <anna.ortiz@novahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-03 09:20:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Final pricing & PO routing — Redwood proposal

Hi Anna,

Thanks for the clear redlines and the VAT certificate. We discussed internally and propose the following to close the order form this week: 

1) Payment terms: Net 60, with a 20% activation prepayment on signature (applies to Year 1 commit). We can accept Net 60 instead of Net 90 to help with your AP timeline.

2) Minimum commit: We are willing to set Year 1 minimum commit to $350,000 (rather than $500,000), with the following guardrails: shortfall billing at renewal OR Redwood may invoice for any early-termination shortfall if the contract terminates before Year 1 ends. Language is in Appendix B (see attached pricing_schedule_nov2026.xlsx).

3) VAT / reverse-charge: We will invoice your UK entity on a reverse-charge basis provided Nova supplies a valid VAT registration and signs the self-billing addendum. Redwood will include explicit indemnity language protecting Redwood from exposures if the VAT documentation is later found invalid. Please confirm the VAT number on the attached certificate.

4) MSA / data residency: We will not amend MSA §5, but will add an order-form acknowledgement of Nova's data residency requirement and commit to providing SOC2 evidence and the relevant control reports within 30 days of signature.

I have uploaded the redlined Order Form (order_form_v4_for_signature.pdf) and prepared a DocuSign envelope for the order form + Appendix B. Link: https://app.docusign.com/link/abc123-orderform

If that works, please confirm and we will route the DocuSign and your PO. If you need a short call to walk through the compromise, Ben and I are available today.

Best regards,
Jordan Blake
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_schedule_nov2026.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Anna Ortiz <anna.ortiz@novahealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement-team@novahealth.com
Date: 2026-12-03 10:03:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Final pricing & PO routing — Redwood proposal

Jordan — thanks for the quick turnaround and the pragmatic solutions. We can accept Net 60 with 20% upfront. Nova will sign the self-billing addendum and provide a signed PO once we receive the DocuSign envelope with the redlined Order Form; we will attach the VAT registration and the company's finance contact on the PO.

Two asks before signature: 
- Please ensure the shortfall billing language is explicitly limited to Year 1 and any early termination events; we won't accept evergreen catch-all billing.
- Can you add an explicit contact for Redwood's billing ops (email for remittance / invoice questions)?

If you can confirm those two points in the DocuSign before we route our PO, we will sign on our side today.

Appreciate the flexibility — Anna
Anna Ortiz
Senior Procurement Manager
Nova Health
